Abstract. A variety of domain-preserving numerical schemes have been developed for scalar stochastic differ-ential equations and for several classes of multidimensional systems, including those defined on hyperrectangles and positive orthants.
Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) are widely used to model dynamical systems subject to random perturbations. In many applications, their solutions must remain in a prescribed domain, such as a positive orthant, a bounded interval, a simplex, or a more general convex domain.
Extending scalar approaches to multidimensional systems requires accounting for interactions between compo-nents, the geometry of the domain and the structure of the noise. Domain-preserving schemes have nevertheless been developed for several classes of stochastic systems [7, 14, 16, 18, 27, 32], with related work on epidemic systems with delays [42]. In particular, [11] proposed a positivity-preserving explicit Milstein-type scheme for stochastic Lotka–Volterra competition systems driven by multidimensional noise and established strong order-one convergence.
Numerical experiments exhibit conver-gence rates close to one over the tested step sizes and include a comparison with the scheme of [6] on a common hypercube problem driven by a scalar Brownian motion. The paper is organized as follows. Section 2 introduces the notation and preliminary inequalities and estab-lishes well-posedness and integrability of the exact solution. Section 3 presents the projected Milstein scheme and proves its strong order-one convergence. Section 4 discusses applications to representative constrained stochastic models.

###### Abstract.
In this work, we propose high-order boundary-preserving numerical schemes for the strong approximation for some scalar stochastic differential equations with invariant domains being open and bounded intervals. The proposed methods involve using the Lamperti transform to map the SDE to another SDE with additive noise with a trivial invariant domain. Then, by imposing regularity assumptions on the original coefficient functions, we can guarantee that the drift coefficient function of the transformed SDE is regular, and known high-order schemes can be used to achieve the desired convergence order.

> Abstract:We develop an explicit domain-preserving projection scheme for scalar stochastic differential equations whose solutions evolve in a prescribed interval. A Lamperti-type transformation converts the original equation into one with additive noise, whose drift may be singular near finite boundaries or grow polynomially at infinity. The proposed domain-preserving projected Euler-Maruyama (DPPEM) scheme combines an explicit Euler-Maruyama step with projection onto a step-size-dependent interior interval.

Under one-sided Lipschitz, boundary, and weighted growth assumptions, with projection parameters chosen according to the coefficient growth and available moment orders, we establish strong order one convergence for admissible moment orders. The analysis combines local consistency and stability estimates with moment and boundary negative moment bounds for the exact solution. Numerical moment bounds follow from the convergence estimate, while numerical negative moment bounds are obtained under additional conditions.

## #1 An explicit domain-preserving projection scheme for scalar stochastic differential equations [PDF] [Copy] [Kimi] [REL]

We develop an explicit domain-preserving projection scheme for scalar stochastic differential equations whose solutions evolve in a prescribed interval. A Lamperti-type transformation converts the original equation into one with additive noise, whose drift may be singular near finite boundaries or grow polynomially at infinity. The proposed domain-preserving projected Euler-Maruyama (DPPEM) scheme combines an explicit Euler-Maruyama step with projection onto a step-size-dependent interior interval. Under one-sided Lipschitz, boundary, and weighted growth assumptions, with projection parameters chosen according to the coefficient growth and available moment orders, we establish strong order one convergence for admissible moment orders. The analysis combines local consistency and stability estimates with moment and boundary negative moment bounds for the exact solution. Numerical moment bounds follow from the convergence estimate, while numerical negative moment bounds are obtained under additional conditions. Estimates for the inverse Lamperti map yield strong order one convergence for the original equations in the CIR, Heston 3/2, CEV, Ait-Sahalia, and bounded interest-rate models under the stated model conditions. Numerical experiments illustrate the predicted convergence rates and compare computational costs with the Lamperti backward Euler-Maruyama scheme.

## #1 An explicit domain-preserving projected Milstein scheme with strong order one for stochastic systems [PDF] [Copy] [Kimi] [REL]

A variety of domain-preserving numerical schemes have been developed for scalar stochastic differential equations and for several classes of multidimensional systems, including those defined on hyperrectangles and positive orthants. To accommodate more general domain constraints, we consider stochastic systems on bounded or unbounded open convex polyhedral domains, where coefficients may exhibit boundary singularities and polynomial growth. Under local regularity, growth and boundary assumptions, we establish well-posedness and integrability estimates for the exact solution. Then we construct an explicit projected Milstein scheme that preserves the domain by applying a Euclidean projection onto a step-size-dependent interior set after each Milstein update. For systems driven by multidimensional commutative noise, we prove strong order-one convergence for the maximum grid error in Lp, for suitable p > 1 and sufficiently small step sizes under additional weighted regularity and stability conditions. The proof combines these integrability estimates with local Milstein consistency, localization and weighted stability, without requiring a priori step-size-uniform moment or boundary inverse-moment bounds for the numerical approximation. Applications to constrained stochastic models and numerical experiments illustrate the observed first-order convergence behavior.

## Abstract

Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with multiple conserved quantities are ubiquitous in scientific fields, modeling systems from molecular dynamics to celestial mechanics. ###### Abstract

We develop an explicit domain-preserving projection scheme for scalar stochastic differential equations whose solutions evolve in a prescribed interval. A Lamperti-type transformation converts the original equation into one with additive noise, whose drift may be singular near finite boundaries or grow polynomially at infinity. The proposed domain-preserving projected Euler–Maruyama (DPPEM) scheme combines an explicit Euler–Maruyama step with projection onto a step-size-dependent interior interval. Under one-sided Lipschitz, boundary, and weighted growth assumptions, with projection parameters chosen according to the coefficient growth and available moment orders, we establish strong order one convergence for admissible moment orders. The analysis combines local consistency and stability estimates with moment and boundary negative moment bounds for the exact solution. Numerical moment bounds follow from the convergence estimate, while numerical negative moment bounds are obtained under additional conditions. Estimates for the inverse Lamperti map yield strong order one convergence for the original equations in the CIR, Heston 3/2, CEV, Aït–Sahalia, and bounded interest-rate models under the stated model conditions. Numerical experiments illustrate the predicted convergence rates and compare computational costs with the Lamperti backward Euler–Maruyama scheme.

keenable.title: Explicit domain preserving numerical schemes for a class of stochastic differential equations
keenable.snippet: We construct and analyze numerical schemes for systems of stochastic differential equations, which preserve almost surely a given hypercube of arbitrary dimension. We propose a new general class of explicit schemes, such that for any choice of the time-step size the numerical solution takes values in the hypercube. We prove strong and weak convergence results for this general class of domain preserving numerical schemes, with strong order $1/2$ and weak order $1$ in general. We also construct a variant of the scheme which achieves strong order $1$ when the stochastic differential equation is driven by a one-dimensional Brownian motion. The convergence results are illustrated with numerical experiments.

# An explicit domain-preserving projected Milstein scheme with strong order one for stochastic systems

A variety of domain-preserving numerical schemes have been developed for scalar stochastic differential equations and for several classes of multidimensional systems, including those defined on hyperrectangles and positive orthants. To accommodate more general domain constraints, we consider stochastic systems on bounded or unbounded open convex polyhedral domains, where coefficients may exhibit boundary singularities and polynomial growth. Under local regularity, growth and boundary assumptions, we establish well-posedness and integrability estimates for the exact solution. Then we construct an explicit projected Milstein scheme that preserves the domain by applying a Euclidean projection onto a step-size-dependent interior set after each Milstein update. For systems driven by multidimensional commutative noise, we prove strong order-one convergence for the maximum grid error in Lp, for suitable p > 1 and sufficiently small step sizes under additional weighted regularity and stability conditions. The proof combines these integrability estimates with local Milstein consistency, localization and weighted stability, without requiring a priori step-size-uniform moment or boundary inverse-moment bounds for the numerical approximation. Applications to constrained stochastic models and numerical experiments illustrate the observed first-order convergence behavior.

1CSQI Chair, École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne, 1015 Lausanne, Switzerland. 2Laboratory of Applied Mechanical Design, École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne, 1015 Lausanne, Switzerland.

In this work, we introduce Euler–Maruyama-based Basis-Update & Galerkin (EM–BUG) dynamical low-rank integrators for stochastic differential equations (SDEs). These integrators extend the standard BUG integrator to the Euler–
Maruyama scheme by incorporating diffusion directions into the augmented physical basis and exploiting the second moment to update the physical basis independently of the new Brownian increments. This construction avoids the inversion of the reduced second-moment matrix and allows us to derive con-vergence estimates that are robust with respect to small eigenvalues. Strong and weak convergence estimates show that the time-discretization accuracy of the underly-ing Euler–Maruyama scheme is preserved up to the low-rank approximation error. We also derive Monte Carlo error estimates recovering the standard sampling rate up to the time-discretization and low-rank approximation errors. Numerical experiments on linear SDEs with additive and multiplicative noise support these theoretical results and demonstrate accuracy comparable to the standard BUG integrator.

Abstract:

In this paper, we study the strong approximation of scalar stochastic differential equations (SDEs), which take values in a domain and have non-Lipschitz coefficients. By combining a Lamperti-type transformation with a semi-implicit discretization approach and a taming strategy, we construct a domain-preserving scheme that strongly converges under weak assumptions. Moreover, we show that this scheme has strong convergence order under additional assumptions on the coefficients of the SDE. In our scheme, the domain preservation is a consequence of the semi-implicit discretization approach, while the taming strategy allows controlling terms of the scheme that admit singularities but are required to obtain the desired order.
Our general convergence results are applied to various SDEs from applications, with sub-linearly or super-linearly growing and non-globally Lipschitz coefficients. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate our theoretical findings.

# An explicit domain-preserving projection scheme for scalar stochastic differential equations
Xingwei Hu·Yaozhong Hu·Aiguo Xiao

## Abstract
We develop an explicit domain-preserving projection scheme for scalar stochastic differential equations whose solutions evolve in a prescribed interval.
A Lamperti-type transformation converts the original equation into one with additive noise, whose drift may be singular near finite boundaries or grow polynomially at infinity.
The proposed domain-preserving projected Euler-Maruyama (DPPEM) scheme combines an explicit Euler-Maruyama step with projection onto a step-size-dependent interior interval.
Under one-sided Lipschitz, boundary, and weighted growth assumptions, with projection parameters chosen according to the coefficient growth and available moment orders, we establish strong order one convergence for admissible moment orders.
The analysis combines local consistency and stability estimates with moment and boundary negative moment bounds for the exact solution.
Numerical moment bounds follow from the convergence estimate, while numerical negative moment bounds are obtained under additional conditions.
Estimates for the inverse Lamperti map yield strong order one convergence for the original equations in the CIR, Heston 3/2, CEV, Ait-Sahalia, and bounded interest-rate models under the stated model conditions.
Numerical experiments illustrate the predicted convergence rates and compare computational costs with the Lamperti backward Euler-Maruyama scheme.

ultimate.title: An explicit domain-preserving projection scheme for scalar stochastic differential equations
ultimate.snippet: We develop an explicit domain-preserving projection scheme for scalar stochastic differential equations whose solutions evolve in a prescribed interval. A Lamperti-type transformation converts the original equation into one with additive noise, whose drift may be singular near finite boundaries or grow polynomially at infinity. The proposed domain-preserving projected Euler-Maruyama (DPPEM) scheme combines an explicit Euler-Maruyama step with projection onto a step-size-dependent interior interval. Under one-sided Lipschitz, boundary, and weighted growth assumptions, with projection parameters chosen according to the coefficient growth and available moment orders, we establish strong order one convergence for admissible moment orders. The analysis combines local consistency and stability estimates with moment and boundary negative moment bounds for the exact solution. Numerical moment bounds follow from the convergence estimate, while numerical negative moment bounds are obtained under additional conditions. Estimates for the inverse Lamperti map yield strong order one convergence for the original equations in the CIR, Heston 3/2, CEV, Ait-Sahalia, and bounded interest-rate models under the stated model conditions. Numerical experiments illustrate the predicted convergence rates and compare computational costs with the Lamperti backward Euler-Maruyama scheme.

ultimate.snippet:
# An explicit domain-preserving projected Milstein scheme with strong order one for stochastic systems

A variety of domain-preserving numerical schemes have been developed for scalar stochastic differential equations and for several classes of multidimensional systems, including those defined on hyperrectangles and positive orthants. To accommodate more general domain constraints, we consider stochastic systems on bounded or unbounded open convex polyhedral domains, where coefficients may exhibit boundary singularities and polynomial growth. Under local regularity, growth and boundary assumptions, we establish well-posedness and integrability estimates for the exact solution. Then we construct an explicit projected Milstein scheme that preserves the domain by applying a Euclidean projection onto a step-size-dependent interior set after each Milstein update. For systems driven by multidimensional commutative noise, we prove strong order-one convergence for the maximum grid error in Lp, for suitable p > 1 and sufficiently small step sizes under additional weighted regularity and stability conditions. The proof combines these integrability estimates with local Milstein consistency, localization and weighted stability, without requiring a priori step-size-uniform moment or boundary inverse-moment bounds for the numerical approximation. Applications to constrained stochastic models and numerical experiments illustrate the observed first-order convergence behavior.

ultimate.title: Explicit domain preserving numerical schemes for a class of stochastic differential equations
ultimate.snippet: We construct and analyze numerical schemes for systems of stochastic differential equations, which preserve almost surely a given hypercube of arbitrary dimension. We propose a new general class of explicit schemes, such that for any choice of the time-step size the numerical solution takes values in the hypercube. We prove strong and weak convergence results for this general class of domain preserving numerical schemes, with strong order $1/2$ and weak order $1$ in general. We also construct a variant of the scheme which achieves strong order $1$ when the stochastic differential equation is driven by a one-dimensional Brownian motion. The convergence results are illustrated with numerical experiments.

Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) are widely used to model dynamical systems subject to random perturbations. In many applications, their solutions must remain in a prescribed domain, such as a positive orthant, a bounded interval, a simplex, or a more general convex domain.

Numerical experiments exhibit conver-gence rates close to one over the tested step sizes and include a comparison with the scheme of [6] on a common hypercube problem driven by a scalar Brownian motion.
